CANONICAL_NAME.value: 4.3BSD-Tahoe TCP (1988) -- slow start, congestion avoidance, Karn's algorithm, RTT variance (Jacobson/Karels)

value.lineage: TCP congestion-control lineage, the HISTORICAL REDESIGN: Van Jacobson and Mike Karels added a congestion window (snd_cwnd), slow start, congestion avoidance (additive increase / multiplicative decrease), Karn's retransmission-timer rule and the mean+variance RTT estimator to 4.3BSD-Tahoe in response to the 1986 collapse. Preserved from unix-history-repo tag BSD-4_3_Tahoe.

value.built_to: make every sender probe for its share of a shared link and back off multiplicatively when loss signals congestion
value.pressure: the 1986 congestion collapse: many senders, shared scarce links, loss as the only feedback
value.success_means: aggregate throughput stays near link capacity; senders converge to a fair share; no collapse

value.pressure: bandwidth scarcity, loss as the only congestion signal, competing flows
value.failure_condition: the 4.2 collapse recurs; or a single sender starves others

value: superseded (direction UNFIXED in Techne's vocabulary; note: 'fast recovery added'): bsd-tcp-4.3-reno-1990

evidence.ref: Fall & Floyd, Simulation-based Comparisons of Tahoe, Reno and SACK TCP, CCR 1996
evidence.says: Compares the variants directly; Tahoe collapses its window to one segment on loss, which Reno's fast recovery avoids.
